name: frozen: orb30 short tight
why: the rule frozen on 10 November: a breakdown of the first 30 minutes' range, with the market falling too; kept here so the frozen choice is tested on real history, not only going forward

name: orb30 short wide
why: sellers who waited for the first half hour push through its low; the far side of the range as the stop makes the charges a smaller share of the risk

name: orb30 long wide
why: the mirror: late buyers chase a break of the first half hour's high (the backtests so far say longs lose: a control)

name: orb30 short wide 3R nifty
why: a breakdown on a falling market day is index selling, which keeps going longer: let it run to 3R

name: orb30 long wide 3R nifty
why: the mirror on a rising market day

name: orb15 stop-entry short
why: a resting stop order fills at the level instead of a bar later: it tests whether being early is what a close entry loses

name: orb15 stop-entry long
why: the mirror of the stop entry: a buy stop resting over the 15-minute high

name: prev-day low break
why: stops sit under yesterday's low; when the market is falling too, their selling carries the break

name: prev-day high break
why: the mirror: buy stops over yesterday's high

name: orb30 long calm VIX
why: in a calm market a range break is less often a fake-out: one regime filter, chosen in advance, not searched

name: last hour long with Nifty
why: on a day Nifty is 0.5 % or more up by 14:30, index funds and derivative books trade the move into NSE's closing price (the average of the last 30 minutes): buy at 14:30, out at 15:10

name: last hour short with Nifty
why: the mirror on a day Nifty is 0.5 % or more down by 14:30
